rule: A push runs in the same Bash call, or the same committed script, as every check on the ref it writes
description: `plugin/governance/security-policy.md` (Shell Identifier Discipline) is the canonical source for the rule that a check made in one Bash call does not carry into the next, so a push runs in the same call, or the same committed script, as every check on the ref it writes. The rule is load-bearing because each Bash call is a fresh shell: a branch or upstream check made in one call and a push made in a later call act on two separate readings of git state, and a change between them can aim the push, or a force-with-lease retry, at a ref the check never saw. The source pin is ONE span carrying the fresh-shell premise (a captured value is used inside the call that captured it, and a later call re-derives it rather than pasting it) and the push obligation with its scope (the same call or the same committed script, and every check on the ref the push writes), so deleting the premise, narrowing `every check` to some checks, or dropping the committed-script alternative or the same-call requirement turns the suite red. Three consumers pin the pointer at each push site, each as the sentence that routes every push through the push-branch script and names the canonical file and section: `plugin/skills/push-branch/SKILL.md` names `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh` by path; `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` step 6 and `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` step 7 name it as the push-branch script. Deleting a pointer or retargeting its file or section turns the suite red. A `set_check` asserts that `plugin/skills/push-branch/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md`, and `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` carry ZERO `git push` command forms, so a raw push added back beside the script invocation is caught as an addition, which no presence pin can see. The capture is anchored on the `git` command word and ends on the `push` subcommand; any global option tokens between them are matched by negated-delimiter classes and captured with the subcommand, so the bare form `git push` counts against the expected zero and an option-prefixed form such as `git -C <dir> push` is an extra that subset mode rejects. The push-branch script itself is deliberately not named in the set_check, because it is the one place a push runs; its behavior is asserted by `tools/test_push_branch.sh`, not by this fixture. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these four word sequences exist in these four named files and that the three named push-site files contain no line the extraction regex matches; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about what an agent actually runs. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the set_check `files` list is literal with no glob expansion, so it is blind to files it does not name, and a `git push` in any other skill, agent, or governance file stays green, per rule 6 of the pin-authoring contract; (2) the pins are presence-only: a NEW push site that never carries the pointer is an absence defect no fixture in this directory can see, per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract; (3) the extraction is line-scoped, so a command split across lines between `git` and `push`, a quoted command word such as `"git" push`, a push run through an alias, a variable, or another wrapper, and any push phrased without the literal `git` and `push` words are invisible; (4) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as surrounding prose that offers a direct push as an alternative to the script, is invisible; (5) the push-branch `## Do Not` line against pushing outside the push script is unpinned.
